reviews.text: I wanted to like this game, but after an hour of play (4 games) there were numerous points that made me unable to see the game offering much replayability. The main issue with the game: 1. Movement - the movement is clunky. Compared to games like crab champions and risk of reign, the movement is slow and completely reliant on the dash ability to dodge anything. 2. Enemies - while there is a good variation of enemies, I could not tell why I was getting hit by them. There wasn't enough telegraphing of their attacks or patterns to work out. Dodge seem to just happen from pressing the dash, rather than any skill. 3. Too Easy - we played with a lot of difficulty multipliers, and it was still too easy. Even with the difficulty in dodging enemy attacks or knowing what is attacking me and how, I never died nor did my co-op mate. 4. Game building was lacking - unlike other roguelites with permadeath, I couldn't see much differentiation in the build types - usually just a case of 3 - 4 abilities that got stronger as the game went on. New mechanics that significiantly varied the build didn't seem to present. There are other reason but these were my main issues with enjoying the game.

As much as I would love to recommend this game, I just can't. I guess. The yellow/crit build/blot thing? It is BEYOND useless. Every other blot does at least twice as much damage at the end of every game when I've played with other people, and you would think crits would be good, but no, not in this game. The summoner/green blot is OVERPOWERED. It does 2-3x as much damage at the end of the game compared to literally any other blot I've seen so far when I've played with others. The art style and visuals are really nice, and I saw some other people complain about performance I think, but it runs just fine for me and I've had no issues performance wise. Another, really, really annoying thing, is that you can't even dodge half the attacks being sent at you. I mean, I might be wrong, but I'd have to be a complete smooth brain because I'm gluing my eyes to my screen and there's so many projectiles I just can't see or that travel too fast and are just.. not, dodgeable. There's no block. No nothing. You rely on a dash or a blink, and the blink has a big cooldown and is cool and all but I've died mid-blink so many times. So not even the dashes/blinks have invulnerability, which is just.. crazy. I've been permanently CC'd by some enemy, I think the one that spawns all the rocks around you continously, and no, I'm not exaggerating. I was STUCK. I could not move. Nothing was around me. I had no status effects. I was STUCK. A revive fixed it but.. like, I guess that's kind of expected with very Early Access games, so it's not .. as big of a deal? I really do hate how enemies continuously outspeed you unless you have movement pages/perks (which are completely RNG lol) and again, you just can't dodge half the attacks. I just fought a final boss that spawned pillars continuously, like four at a time and even after destroying one, another one pops up IMMEDIATELY after, and they all shoot tracking projectiles towards you, that I can't dodge. I can blink, sure. But then they just turn back around and head straight to me. It's CANCER. I like this game, and I know it has potential, but it just feels.. so bad to play. I'll keep at it and maybe it's all just a "skill issue" but it really.. really does not feel or seem that way. Literally not one thing I've said here has been even SLIGHTLY exaggerated, it really feels that bad. But I guess it's still kinda... fun? Also.. like, upgrades don't.. feel that impactful. Idk, it's just.. not that fun for me. TL;DR - Extremely hard, even impossible to dodge attacks from enemies, very, very consistently - Movement does NOT feel good - You can't even dodge half of the attacks - Some of the bosses are literal cancer to fight - Very poorly balanced between "classes"/"blots" (in order from strongest from what I've seen: Green (Stupid OP), Blue (or Red, can't tell), Red (or Blue, can't tell), and then Yellow consistently being at the bottom in damage. The Green blot's minion does more damage ALONE than I can with yellow, regardless of how good of upgrades I get - Upgrades kind of suck and don't feel very impactful for the most part. HOWEVER, it has some.. pros? - It has a good amount of content for how early of a build this is - Unique and nice visuals - Nice, very short runs compared to almost every other roguelike/roguelite - Decent cosmetics Please keep up the good work and address said issues cause I sure as hell know I'm not imagining things lol. Crab Champions, Gunfire Reborn, RoboQuest, and Risk of Rain all feel infinitely better to play..

The game is pretty fun for the first few hours, but the going from difficulty0 -> difficulty 20+, there is really no tangible change. The meta-debuffs you choose for yourself are negligible and barely noticed, and the buffs you give the enemies feel similar. Too much happens on the screen because of the black/white coloring of the enemies that makes them hard to identify as more and more enemies spawn. Game ends up becoming 'aoe the thing, dance around to not die or just go leech build and dont die while the entire map hits you'. The game has a lot of 'passive/conditional' buffs, way more than things that make your active skills feel different and play differently: "Consecutive hits do bonus damage" "Full mana = more damage" "Empty shield or full shield = more damage" "Press your skill, and this thing happens" Nothing groundbreaking here like Gunfire Reborn where a build can feel vastly different game to game because there are core impact skills that modify how you'd play - this game is hold left click, click right click. The skill concepts and the 'levels' are unique, and the game has potential but if the core loop is cemented as what it is now, I'd recc against buying it.

Pretty cool game, but there is one mechanic that really feels out of place. This game has something called Prestige, which allows you to go reset your progress for some really unnotable changes. I don't think I would honestly care all that much about it if not for the detriment it causes to the game. (this talks about the prestige mechanic, although as the devs have commented, they have made strides to improve it later in time after I had interacted with the system.) So I played this game with a good friend of mine, and at some point we both hit prestige at the same time. Then, suddenly, all the spells, signature inks, tomes, etc, all of it got undone. You might think that this is normal, plenty of games have a similar resetting mechanic, but in those games you get a tangible benefit that makes getting back easier. This game doesn't have that. Its basically just a full reset button that puts a number next to your name for the amount of times you have pressed it. Now maybe this was changed since we last played, but this reset basically caused us to completely drop the game since everything we had been working to unlock (spells, tomes, inks, all progression, etc) was brushed away with nothing to show for it. It honestly felt really demoralizing and disheartening, and I feel like the creators only included this as a token way to try and extend the game's runtime since you really only get to this point once you have reached the end of the game. I have since returned and grinded my way back up almost to the second prestige, but I would never willingly press that button now that I have gone through its pains once. The whole game is fun because of the many combinations you can make. Even in just the hub area, you can choose three unique spells to equip, a signature ink which massively changes the gameplay, various passive upgrades which you can only enable a select few of at a given time, to play from many different tomes (basically levels), and many different modifiers for the tomes to make them more challenging in unique ways. Its really fun, and you unlock these through playing the game, but prestige kicks you down by removing all this choice. I have no idea how the creators thought this was a good idea. The only other real kinda gripe I have with this game is the performance. Now I have some real beefy hardware, for the current time at least, im talking a RTX4060 and similarly powerful other components, yet with all this power, the inevitably game drops to 10 fps or lower after playing in the endless mode for a few loops. Its not a graphics issue, it has to do with unoptimised code. Maybe this was just happening because I used a sort of flamethrower type thing on my primary weapon, but whenever I attacked my fps would drop from in the hundreds down to 10. Actually one other thing, some of the balancing seems really non-existent. The red signature ink (letting you drian health from enemies), the yellow ink (dealing massive damage, at least doubling it but can easily go way higher with items), and the orange ink (giving you a turret that also heals you), are just objectively much better to use than something like the green ink (gives you a random follower which shoots at stuff) or cyan ink (gives you armor that you cna sacrifice to deal damage). This game has a big problem around healing really, most things in the game deal a lot of damage (on high difficulty levels at least) but you almost never get things to heal you (unless you are really lucky with your item spawns), forcing you to really only use 'meta' inks since you just die otherwise. Maybe its a skill issue, I dont know, but I hate that I feel like I need to use red, yellow, or orange inks in order to be able to play the game with any kind of effectiveness. I like the ideas of the other inks, but they simply dont have the survivability required in order to keep up. But other than those things, honestly a fun game,

I was having a fantastic time with the game, from the colored Ink system, to the spell combinations, and especially the beautiful aesthetic, all up until I encountered the bonus objective "Catch the Golden Ink." A Harry Potter reference, [i]in 2025[/i], is incredibly disappointing to see, and it shows, at best, the devs' ignorance to the unrivaled damage its creator has done to transgender rights. Can no longer in good faith recommend this game, and will be advising friends to steer clear. There are plenty of other roguelikes out there to spend your time with.

The idea behind the game is great - but that's where anything positive I have to say about the game ends. Movement and attacks feel slow and clunky. Something about the visuals are off, making the entire game feel old and, worse; dated. Most of the unlocks are boring. Both the player characters and the enemies lack any kind of personality. A lot of the damage is entirely unavoidable which, combined with enemies that almost completely removes your movement speed, makes the entire game experience frustrating and downright unpleasant. The combat arenas are tiny and uninteresting. The mini-games between the combat levels add nothing fun to the game except making each run drag on for longer. I love this genre; both roguelikes and third person action games. This game? No. I'm uninstalling and putting it in the "Just forget you own it"-collection. I've rarely been so surprised at a game's positive reviews, but this game is so bad that I look at disbelief at its (currently) Very Positive review rating.

Vellum looks great, the art style is wonderful, and I do think there is fun to be had with it. However as an actual game, I think there are serious design flaws that negatively affect everything. No better example comes to mind than the sword weapon, it truly showcases how HORRENDOUS the game design can be. It is impossible to no-hit any level with the amount of screen vomit at once, why is this a problem? This forces players, especially sword users, to use life-drain which in a roguelike, you should never be FORCED to go into a specific build just to make your weapon work, and it should NEVER be impossible to no-hit. I urge you to check out Crab Champions, Gunfire Reborn, other roguelikes that do a similar concept but execute it way better. So, I just complained about it being impossible to no-hit, but that doesn't mean the game is exactly hard either. I don't think I've lost a single run in my almost 5 hours of Vellum, not because I'm good at it, but because I think the game is too easy. Unless you really stack the difficulty modifiers, it feels almost impossible to lose. I remember activating torn pages and being kinda scared of the consequence of it, but it never really punishes me for any torn page I activate as I still can easily beat the run. Overall I think it's quite a flawed game, it allures you in with the cool art style, and the cool design of the weapons. Once you start sinking your teeth into it though you really notice the problems. Also please for the love of god change the music up.

[h1][b]神笔战魑魅，挥墨驱魍魉[/b][/h1] 《Vellum》是一款特别的3D弹幕肉鸽游戏，玩家将化身一只魔法笔，使用神奇的墨水之力，进入魔法书对抗各类污染和怪物，守护巨大的图书馆和书中世界。 本作的主角是一支幻化为人形的魔法笔，其浮空而立，一手法典一手弹幕颇有战斗法师的感觉。 游戏的目标是进入一个个书中世界，清除为祸其中的妖物，每个书籍的流程都包含多个关卡，这些关卡范围并不大，敌人会从天而降袭击而来，因此无需到处寻敌，但也因此少了几分探索的感觉。 游戏打造了多达7种颜色的墨水，这便是不同的战斗风格了，其中： 蓝色墨水为持续性dot伤害、黄色墨水持续发射可以附带增伤效果、绿色墨水可以召唤出墨宠一同作战、红色墨水附带吸血效果、橙色墨水可以放置一座炮台自动杀敌。 本作的战斗系统为TPS射击，角色一共有普通攻击、主动技能、移动技能、特殊技能等4种操作和输出方式。 其中普攻可以不断累积法力值，就是角色右侧的三个六边形图标了，法力值可用来释放主动技能，如果其累积满之后继续攻击敌人，还可转换为匹配当前战斗风格的法力图标，效果更强。 随着不断游戏，使用获得的资源可以在图书馆解锁上述内容的更多备选项，搭配构筑能带来各种不一样的游戏体验。 每次通过关卡后可进行三选一的构筑，游戏打造了超过300种卷轴和100多种升级，混搭这些内容可创造千变万化的战斗风格。 此外部分关卡开始前还需要选择负面效果，诸如增强敌人、Boss等，这个玩法的加入比较考验玩家对战局的理解，如何做到最小化负面效果是本作的必修课。 《Vellum》整体手感不错，颇有《雨中冒险2》的感觉，需要注意的是敌人的弹道和行动都很迅速，因此战斗中务必要动起来，要不然很容易暴毙。 本作还支持最多4人联机游玩，目前唯一的不足是只有英文，期待汉化的加入。 [quote]热爱游戏，畅玩游戏，分享游戏，专注鉴赏评测与深度解析 欢迎关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44110339/]游理游据[/url]，走进游戏世界，品味第九艺术[/quote]
相当充足的内容量。值得一试。

Far too buggy to recommend in the current state. The chapters are very short, and it only takes a few bosses into the run for scrolls to stop working and desyncing to occur. The levels also start taking too long to load, getting worse the longer the run goes on. Sometimes it takes almost a minute of standing around in a level before you get to choose the next difficulty modifier, which is before enemies even can spawn in. This is supposed to be a few seconds after loading too, so you know something is going very wrong on the backend. Also forgot to mention the disconnects, which ruin runs. If disconnected, you can't rejoin until the next non-combat section. You lose out on the upgrades you would have had, and the points to invest into your perks for the run.

Can't say I recommend this one. One of the main methods the game uses to increase the difficulty is just to decrease the contrast you get on the screen, making it more difficult to identify hazards from other parts of the stages. I don't really like it when a game uses accessibility downgrades as a crutch to spike difficulty.

I'm trying really hard to like it,but it's kind of boring to be honest. This WOULD very much be a "check back after early access" review... But this is full release. The combat is the entire game. There is nothing outside of combat. Except really minimal exploration. And it's...not great. Attacks have no weight, from players OR enemies. Combat is kind of slow and just ... Eh? Boss designs are boring, uninspire, and incredibly easy. The only "hard" thing about the game comes from, weirdly, bad color design? Despite being a game where color is literally a huge focus of the game. (Enemy bombs and stuff like that are white, which makes them hard to notice... Not that it matters they do almost no damage.) The few little platforming/exploration areas and just how incredibly "meh" the combat is makes me wonder if the game was even play tested. Increase enemy aggression, add flinching and very minor knock back to attacks, both to AND from players, increase attack speed across the board from both players and enemies, shorter the dodge cool downs to compensate, and make enemy attacks red and more clearly visible and the game will be a million times better. It has the same major issue that Risk of Rain does. It tries to cover up how boring the combat is by throwing 10x more enemies than it needs at you, but, like ROR, that doesn't even make the combat challenging or fun. Just tedious. That said, the loading screens are AMAZINGLY seamless, and the roguelike currency systems are fairly interesting (though each class frankly needs more varied options. After 2 total runs I already bought every spell that remotely sounds fun to use.) The run modifiers are a good idea, but poorly implemented, that has potential tho. Then there's fact that a chapter (basically a chapter is equivalent to a room in most roguelikes) ends INSTANTLY the exact frame the last enemy dies with no chance or option collect the loot laying on the ground is insane. You have to just blindly grab what ever drops and pray it's good for your build otherwise you just outright lose your loot...which is extra absurd when you realize the game is designed around co-op play. Idk. If this was an early access game, I would be saying check it out but keep expectations low till full release. How ever, since this IS full release I can't really recommend it. It's just, ultimately, really hecking boring. Which is a shame because the ideas and concepts are there. It just REALLY needed to cook a little longer and definitely needed a lot more play testing before release. Edit: I'm actually laughing going back and reading other people's reviews, and seeing that everyone else is comparing it to Risk or Rain as well but in a good way. The ONLY similarity to Risk of Ran is the fact that there are way more enemies on screen than needed, and like RoR, said enemies do almost 0 damage while taking longer to kill than they should. This is NOT a positive. The similarities to Risk of Rain are literally only the bad parts of RoR. Edit 2: Also the people saying the roguelike elements and deep, complex and full of variety are straight up lying to you. There are like 6 classes total. Each one has 3 spell categories and roughly 10 spells per category. That might sound nice on paper, but basically every category of every class only has basically a single spell you'll ever use. What ever your playstyle will be. The other stuff will just prove straight up bad. As for the roguelike progression... In game you get to pick from 3 perks, twice each "chapter". By the 3rd chapter (each run is like 5 or 6 chapters) you'll will already start seeing perks repeat. There is almost ZERO depth, and you'll end a run with the same build every time.

Vellum is an stage-based action roguelike where you use a variety of purchasable spells bound to your primary, secondary, dash, and ultimate (ink) ability/passive to defeat waves of enemies while occasionally exploring levels to unlock more upgrades in the run. The gameplay loop is relatively simple: select your 4-part loadout, defeat the enemies, explore a few stages, and defeat the boss all while dealing with enemy modifiers of your choice that add a challenge and also choose from a selection of buffs that augment your play-style to deal more damage. The game itself is decent and can be fun, but the loadout system suffers in this game and it feels like there were missed opportunities to add more replayability. However, if you like the simplistic nature of the game, it may be fun to play it out over and over again. Pros: - The game looks and sounds good - Enemy design and diversity is interesting to play around - Lots of upgrades in a run to deal more damage Cons: - The spells are plentiful, but that does not mean that they offer much variance. Despite the many combinations of builds the game offers, there are really 2-3 ways to play this game. Ranged or Melee, you can combine them, but I do not see why you would necessarily want to. All ranged spells do not act the same. The playstyle, however, feels rather samey. This changes with melee spells, but you can operate the same way with the right ultimate passive. - The color palette is nice, but the Area of Effects the game tends to use lack real warning, urgency, and contrast, for example, using a white warning area to show some attacks feel very off in a game full of visual clutter when enemies get plentiful. Personal Gripes: - The combat loops are very repetitive and underwhelming, even if you do lots of damage with your upgrades. The combat loop devolves into the same actions you will take over and over again and it got old very fast for me since there was very little thought behind my actions. You need to build up charges to use your secondary spell by hitting enemies with your primary spell or you can build up the charges further into empowered charges by hitting enemies even more with your primary spell. So you hold left click until you can use an empowered right click. Your ultimate is on a cooldown, so you can use that on cooldown and your only other ability is your dash which is mainly for evasion. - No matter how cool the upgrades are in a run, it does not take away from the fact that you are doing the same thing and will continue to execute the same game plan of building up your secondary spell with your primary spell. It works, but feels very limiting...I would rather have many different spells you find in a run on a cooldown or maybe have this kind of play style be gated behind one of the ultimate passives or secondary spells instead. These upgrades from what I have seen always tend to bolster your spells or augment them in some way...but all the augments tend to lean towards what is already expected to deal the most damage...charge your secondary with your primary. - Comparisons to games like Risk of Rain 2 are definitely not 100% valid here in my opinion because for starters RoR2 associates risk with all means of getting stronger. Secondly, because the builds are based on your character kit and massive selection of items you pick up in RoR2, whereas this game offers random items that give you some kind of conditional buff while always bolstering the play-style of your character. There is very little risk in a playthrough Vellum with regards to buffing your character, which makes it not as interesting especially in the first few hours of play while buying whatever spells and inks you can buy for a loadout. All-in-all. I would say the game has a lack of variance in the runs to be worth playing over a longer period of time even with all the spells, mutators, and enemy buffs they offer. My first attempt felt very boring to play through with a ranged setup. My second attempt had difficulty modifiers with a melee setup and I was still not feeling very engaged. I know that there are people who will enjoy the simplistic nature of the game though. So even if its not for me, I am sure others will take to it.

Been playing this game exclusively two player and it's been amazing. We're avoiding guides to find things for ourselves and it's been so fun. Clearing levels can add new things to your home base, which gives a really cool feeling of progression. Things are unlocking at a good speed, enough that we have to work for it but not so dragged out we lose patience (we're both notoriously low on attention span so this may be a very quick unlock chain by most people's standards). The puzzles aren't *hard* but they do take a minute or two to work out - I wouldn't call it a puzzle game by any stretch so if that's your jam you won't find it here, but they break up the game nicely. Some levels also have mini games for bonus rewards which are fun. The different classes (inks) are all distinct, even if you're using the same spells, which is cool. (And if you're someone who goes deeper into builds and picks different spells for each colour I imagine it pays off really well). The powerups you get each run feel really impactful, and the overall progression of your character level adds some nice bonuses in terms of basic bonuses (5% more damage, etc) and more specialised passives. We've just unlocked some more game modes too which adds variety to our rotations. Definitely a good game to play with friends. While I'm sure it *could* be done solo it's more fun with allies and some of the bonuses you can pick affect other players as well so there's a stats reason for it. But mostly because it's just such a fun world to share. Everything is very pretty too. No frame rate issues and while I can be a bit of a graphics snob and wish things were higher poly the aesthetic and cohesion of the whole game really makes it a non-issue. Overall a game with a huge amount of customisation, in build and appearance, with a lot of cute odds and ends that really bring the world to life and show that they really thought about player experience in this. Well worth the money, I wouldn't hesitate to recommend this.
